text:
Claire (AE): Quick Q — ACME POC asked for 7yr audit log retention + HSM-backed keys. Are those shipped as a single compliance SKU or separate billable items? Need a line-item level answer to include in the partner quote.

Marco (Solutions): We split them. Base audit logging (30d) is included for enterprise. Anything >90d is the audit-retention add-on (billed per GB-month). HSM/KMS (BYOK) is a separate security add-on — one-time setup + monthly management fee.

Priya (CS): For HIPAA customers we also surface the HIPAA package (DPA + controls + monitoring). HIPAA itself is a compliance/legal package; audit retention and HSM remain separate billables.

Claire (AE): Got it. Can you put numbers? Customer wants to see rough monthly cost and any one-time fees so partner can finalize quote.

Marco (Solutions): Numbers (ballpark for quoting):
- audit-retention: $0.020 per GB-month for hot/nearline (30d-1y)
- cold/archival tier (>1y): $0.005 per GB-month (suitable for 7yr)
- HSM/KMS: $10,000 one-time setup + $500/month management (this covers HSM provisioning + attestation)
- HIPAA package: $2,000/month (includes DPA, monitoring tweaks, attestation support)
- SOC2: included on enterprise plans, no extra SKU unless extended retention requested.

Priya (CS): Also call out egress/export costs if they want data shipped out for archives — standard S3 egress rates apply to exported logs.

Ethan (SalesOps): If Claire needs a discount for a commit-sized deal, include commit amounts/term. Typical concessions: 10-15% off recurring add-ons at ~$100k+ ARR commit; 20%+ requires Deal Desk + RevOps signoff.

Claire (AE): Customer is proposing a 12mo commit that lands ~150k ARR. They asked if we can waive the $10k HSM setup or stretch it over the term. Thoughts?

Ethan (SalesOps): For $150k ARR we can stretch the one-time setup over the term (capitalized) and consider waiving up to 50% of the setup fee with exec approval. Full waiver needs senior approval. Please log the exact ask (ARR, term, margin) and I'll open the Deal Desk thread.

Marco (Solutions): Operational note — if they want HSM-backed keys for HIPAA data residency we must also add the "customer-managed keys" checkbox in the Private deployment config. That has a separate security review (2-3 business days).

Claire (AE): Example quote lines they'd like to see (please confirm formatting):
```
- Audit retention (7yr cold): 12,000 GB x $0.005/GB-month = $600/month
- HSM Setup (one-time): $10,000 (or capitalized over 12 months = $833/mo)
- HSM Management: $500/month
- HIPAA package: $2,000/month
```

Marco (Solutions): That formatting looks good. Call out that cold tier pricing assumes immutable storage and that restores >30d may incur retrieval fees.

Priya (CS): Also include a clause that long-term retention beyond 1 year requires an approved retention policy and may be subject to audit and export controls. Legal should review any country-specific retention mandates.

Claire (AE): @Ethan can you start the Deal Desk request with these numbers and ask for 50% HSM setup waiver as a starting negotiation point? I'll attach the customer's POC sizing. :thumbsup:

Ethan (SalesOps): On it — I'll create the Deal Desk ticket and loop in RevOps + Legal. @LegalBot please flag any DPA or export constraints we need to call out for EU/UK customers.

LegalBot: Noted. If they're EU-based and want 7yr retention, we need to validate lawful basis + DPA amendments. Also check if the customer requires HSM attestations (FIPS/HSM model) — we can provide our HSM vendor certs.

Claire (AE): Thanks all. I'll push the partner quote with the two price options (one with setup capitalized, one with full upfront) and attach RevOps ask. Will report back after Deal Desk. :pray:

Marco (Solutions): Ping me if they want an architecture note for the POC (how logs get shuttled to cold tier + retrieval flow). I can draft a 1-pager.

Priya (CS): I'll prepare the HIPAA onboarding checklist in case they sign.

Claire (AE): Awesome — closing this thread for now.

[reaction] Marco (Solutions): :thumbsup:
[reaction] Ethan (SalesOps): :white_check_mark:
